Round 287 — native expert Copy2D cohort source/lifetime review
Date: 2026-10-12
Scope: read-only source review of `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/perf-prefill-native-copy-cohorts-20261012`. No code was run, built, tested, or changed. Findings below are source analysis, not runtime qualification.

## Conclusion
The inspected path has explicit checks for actual Host-USM provenance, one-allocation extent, device ring ownership, contiguous expert and device-slot layout, event dependencies for every overwritten slot, and release/acquire publication of issued work. Its normal and exception paths drain producer and both queues before stager state retires. I found no source-level admission, event-order, or operand-lifetime defect in those reviewed paths.

The concrete gap is integration evidence: existing CPU tests prove geometry predicates only; the GPU fixture proves one 4-row copy/dependency/padding case with a directly allocated host-USM source. Neither exercises the actual `ArenaExpertSource`/`PinnedArena` ownership proof, owned staging-ring admission, a 16-row/tail/wrap boundary, nor failure/drain behavior. Until those are covered, source review does not establish the complete runtime contract.

## Admission and real allocation ownership
`prefill.cpp:858-875` sets `stage_ring_owned` only when `o.base == nullptr`, then obtains all slots from one `o.take<uint8_t>(ring * MMQ_SLOT)` allocation and lays out slot pointers at `ring_base + i * MMQ_SLOT`. Borrowed-region slots use separate allocations and cannot enter cohort mode. The cohort predicate at `1469-1487` additionally requires the environment switch, an owned ring, no model ring, direct (non-job) source, valid row width/pitches, and no queue capture. Candidate height is bounded by 16, remaining sequence entries, and ring tail. It stops on a job, nonadjacent layer/expert/source address, or nonadjacent destination slot. It then asks `m.src->copy_range` for the contiguous source extent and checks exact first pointer, Host-USM pointer type, source allocation remainder, destination ring extent, slot index, and remaining credits via `copy_cohort_fits`.

`ArenaExpertSource::copy_range` (`src/core/expert_source.cpp:2700-2712`) restricts layer/expert/count and requires `PinnedArena::host_usm_range` to prove that the requested byte span falls in a registered piece; it returns the allocation base and extent. This is stronger than merely observing a pinned or aligned pointer. The GPU wrapper (`src/core/gpu.cpp:274-283`) independently requires source Host-USM and destination Device-USM in the copy queue context, the destination allocation's device to match that queue, and bounded nonzero geometry/pitches. These checks establish allocation provenance in source; they do not prove the runtime's actual USM registration behavior on a particular device without execution.

## Dependencies and publication
For each row, `prefill.cpp:1491-1501` passes the current `m.used[m.used_of[slot]]` event when that slot is live, and supplies a non-null completion-event association. `gpu.cpp:284-300` validates each association, copies every present last-reader event into the dependency vector, submits one `ext_oneapi_memcpy2d`, records metadata, and associates the returned event with every row before returning. The caller only marks rows live and release-publishes the new issued index after return (`prefill.cpp:1503-1511`, `1573-1587`). A consumer waits for the acquire-published issued index and returns credits with a release store (`1597-1605`); the issuer reads consumed credits with acquire semantics (`1577-1584`). Thus each overwritten live slot's last reader is a dependency, all row completions share the submitted event, and consumers cannot observe a partially associated cohort through the published index.

One subtle contract to preserve: the wrapper records the event before assigning `done[row]->ev`. If service-event recording throws after queue submission, the wrapper returns failure without associations; caller performs no retry (`1503` comment) and the issuer fails closed. The thread's catch captures the failure and stops/cancels staging (`1588-1591`), while `IssuerJoin` joins then drains both compute and copy queues (`1558-1570`). This is safe only because unwinding must retain all relevant source/ring/event objects until those drains complete; the inspected RAII order supports that: `IssuerJoin` is declared after `StagerDone`, so it is destroyed first, and the earlier `StagerDone` also cancels and drains before finishing (`1439-1459`). No retry is attempted after an enqueue may have happened.

## Test evidence and remaining contract coverage
`tests/core/copy_cohort_test.cpp` covers pure adjacency, size/credit/ring-wrap arithmetic and overflow using compile-time assertions. It has no `copy_range` or allocation-owner fixture. `tools/test_copy_cohort_gpu.cpp` (`10-46`) directly allocates host/device USM, checks a 4-row pitched copy, per-row prior-reader dependencies, padding/canaries, and the one-row 1D fallback. It does not create an `ArenaExpertSource`, verify a source span crossing or ending at a real `PinnedArena` allocation boundary, or distinguish transient pinned memory from host-USM. Its failure branch syncs both queues before returning and exits immediately if either drain fails (`47-52`); it does not test injected asynchronous faults or post-enqueue event-association failure. CMake registers the CPU test at `894-896`; the GPU fixture target is declared at `450-451` (source declaration alone is not evidence it ran).

Minimal missing fixtures before treating the feature as qualified:
1. A source-contract fixture around `ArenaExpertSource::copy_range` backed by actual host-USM allocations: valid same-piece range; exact allocation-end range; crossing piece/allocation; transient or pinned-but-not-USM rejection; and count/layer/expert boundary. Assert returned base/extent and rejection outcomes.
2. Admission integration at cohort heights 2 and 16, then a short sequence tail and ring-tail boundary. Assert a valid owned single-allocation stage ring admits; borrowed/per-slot ring, resident-cache gaps, cross-layer ranges, insufficient credit, and wrap fall back to one-row copies without issuing a 2D command.
3. Lifecycle fault coverage: producer sees every slot's last-reader dependency; all rows receive the same completion event before issued publication; failure after a possible enqueue never retries and retains source/ring/stager storage through both queue drains. If deterministic event-association injection is infeasible, document that limit and keep an explicit runtime fault test as a release gate.

These are validation gaps, not proof that the current implementation fails. Keep status as source-reviewed/unverified until the fixtures and owner-authorized runtime evidence exist.
